message.content:
The volume \(V\) of a right circular cone is calculated using  

\[
V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{\,2}h .
\]

For a base radius \(r = 3 \text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 5 \text{ cm}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
V &= \tfrac{1}{3}\,\pi(3)^2(5)\\[4pt]
&= \tfrac{1}{3}\,\pi(9)(5)\\[4pt]
&= \tfrac{1}{3}\,\pi(45)\\[4pt]
&= 15\pi \;\text{cm}^{3}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Numerically,

\[
15\pi \approx 15\times 3.14159 \approx 47.12 \text{ cm}^{3}.
\]

So the cone’s volume is **\(15\pi\) cubic centimetres** (about **47.12 cm³**).
